$comment: ★★★ A STATIC `&&label` TABLE LAID OUT AFTER A BLOCK-INSERTING PASS (P69, D-LIR-DESCRIPTOR-BLOCK-IDS-SHIFTED-BY-A-BLOCK-INSERTING-PASS). `static void *const tbl[] = {&&L0, &&L1, &&L2}; goto *tbl[i];` reads the label addresses out of DATA, so no instruction names the blocks: the pipeline binds each label's symbol after assembly, by MIR→LIR's block id, to the FINAL module's offsets (LirBlockSymbolBinding). A block id is an arena position, so every block a later pass inserts renumbers every block after it — an inline-asm template's label, and under a calling convention that walks the guard page, each runtime stack descent's walk. Shapes, each its own exit bit: a table BEFORE both (the control, 1), the template's loop (2), a table in a function after the template's (4), a template and a table in one function (8), a VLA frame (16), a table in a function after the VLA's (64), a VLA and a table in one function (128). ✔MEASURED 2026-10-07 on the build at 71648598 (the probe shape of bit 4): DSS REFUSED it — K_NoMatchingObjectFormat, 'a static initializer takes the address of block 3 … but the assembler published no byte offset for it' — on pe and elf, while gcc and clang (c2x) and mingw gcc ran it to 42 (gnu report ref-gnu-20261007-110448-688ad580, mingw run 20261007-110516-eb0d1c91; `-pedantic-errors` refuses `&&label` on all three, as the GNU extension it is), and the BEFORE control was 42 everywhere. The bits 64 and 128 shapes exist only on a target whose calling convention walks the guard page (pe64); elsewhere they are controls.
